senses: foliage, ears, blades, stalks of trees, grass (as though resembling hair)
la:noun:coma.html:
cŏma, ae, f., = κόμη,
the hair of the head (hence barba comaeque, ), considered as an ornament for the head: comae dicuntur capilli cum aliquā curā compositi, Paul. ex Müll. (class., esp. in poetry and post-Aug. prose; very rare in Cic.).—With adj.: unguentis effluens calamistrata coma,: madens,: fulva, ξανθή, : flava,; : myrtea,: longa,: nitidae, cf.: spissā te nitidum. : odorata,; cf. ambrosiae,: cana,: virides Nereidum,: regia (of Berenice),: ventis horrida facta,; cf.: dare diffundere ventis,. —With verb: deciderint comae,: ne comae turbarentur, quas componi post paulum vetuit. : componere,: comere,; cf.: inustas comere acu,:

pectere, : in gradus frangere,; cf.: formare in gradum,: longam renodare,; cf. : positu variare,; cf. ponere,: componere,: rutilare et summittere (after the manner of the Germans),: sertis implicare,: Delphicā lauro cingere,; cf. in a Gr. constr.: fronde comas vincti,: scindens dolore intonsam comam, Att. ap. (transl. of Hom. Il. 10, 15).—So of Venus lamenting Adonis: effusā isse comā,and in a Gr. constr.: scissa comam,; cf. ; ; ; .—

Of animals, of the golden fleece: agnus aureā clarus comā, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 211 Rib.); cf. .—The mane of lions, ; of the horse,.—*
The crest of a helmet, .—
Transf., of objects resembling the hair in appearance or in ornamental effect; most freq. acc. to a trope common in most languages, of leaves, grass, etc., foliage, ears, grass, and stalks of trees, etc., ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; , ; ; .—
The wool or hair upon parchment, .—Poet., of the rays of light, ; ; ; .
